Off-site destinations are now set up once and offered to every domain. A wizard lists every service BombVault can write to, from S3 storage services and your own S3 server to SFTP, WebDAV and the cloud drives rclone supports, and walks through the sign-in, a connection test and the folder. On every card the placement becomes a row of buttons: **Local** and one per off-site target, and the lit ones get the backups. Everything you set up before keeps working as it is.

## ✨ Added

### Destinations

- **Set up once, used everywhere.** **Settings, Off-site, Destinations** holds the places off-site copies go. A destination shows up as a button in the placement row of every domain and item, and the first time it is ticked for a domain, BombVault creates that domain's repository in a folder under it.
- **Every service in one list.** The wizard shows each service with its logo, in four groups: storage services with S3 buckets (Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Cloudflare R2, Hetzner Object Storage, Amazon S3 and others), your own S3 server (Garage, SeaweedFS, RustFS, Ceph, JuiceFS, Versity S3 Gateway), your own server and shares (rest-server, Hetzner Storage Box, SFTP, SMB, WebDAV, a mounted path), and cloud storage (OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, pCloud, Nextcloud and the rest rclone supports). Each says how well it suits backups, and cloud drives say that the first backup and pruning take longer there.
- **The sign-in each service needs.** An access key for S3, a user and password for WebDAV and SMB, an app password where two-factor sign-in blocks the normal one, BombVault's public SSH key for SFTP and the Storage Box, and for services that sign in through a browser an `rclone authorize` command to run on a computer that has one, with a field for the token it prints.
- **Test, then pick the folder.** **Test connection** checks the sign-in before anything is saved. The folder step lists the folders on the destination, creates one with **New folder**, and shows the free space where the service reports it.
- **A straight answer on delete protection.** The wizard says what the service can do: a rest-server in append-only mode refuses deletion and the tamper test checks it, an S3 bucket can keep old versions with versioning and object lock, and a cloud drive cannot refuse deletion at all.
- **The right route for each service.** S3 services use restic's own S3 backend, so a storage class and object lock apply. Every other service runs through the rclone BombVault ships, and its remote appears in the rclone config under Settings, Cloud access.
- **Ready for an emergency.** The recovery kit lists every destination with the repository of each domain under it. A settings export carries the destinations, and with credentials included their sign-in as well.

### Placement as a row of buttons

- **Light what should get the backups.** Each container, VM and folder set card has **Local** and one button per off-site target of its domain. With Local lit, the item is written to its local repository and copied to every other lit target.
- **Off-site without Local.** With Local dark, the item is written straight to the direct repository of the first lit target and copied from there to the other lit targets. The first time, a dialog creates that direct repository.
- **New destinations are one click away.** The row also shows the destinations the domain has no target under yet. A click creates the domain's target and lights it for this item only; every other item starts without a copy there.
- **Placement defaults use the same row**, under Settings, Storage, Placement defaults.

## 🎨 Changed

- **The three placement segments are gone.** Local, Local + off-site and Off-site only, the **Copy to** chips and the **Send to** list are replaced by the row of buttons. One button always stays lit, because a backup needs a place to go; to leave something out of backups, exclude it.
- **A target made from a destination follows it.** Its name, location, credentials, storage class and immutable switch come from the destination and are locked in the domain's list, which says which destination it came from. Retention, compression and growth budget stay per domain.
- **Add a target for this domain only.** The button under each domain's off-site targets is renamed, since it adds a target by hand-typed URL for that domain alone.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Copies from a direct repository.** An item on a direct repository is copied to the other targets with that repository's own credentials, never to the target it belongs to, and the copies age like the item's other off-site snapshots.
- **The primary off-site target is probed with its own credentials** when it uses a credential set of its own.

## 🌐 Translations

- The destinations card and wizard, the row of buttons and every new message in all 42 languages.
- Destinations and the new placement row in all 26 documentation languages, on the off-site and recovery, features and configuration pages.

## Upgrading

- **Nothing has to be changed.** The database is upgraded on the first start, every item keeps its placement and every target keeps replicating as before. Settings export files from older versions still import and leave the destinations alone.
- **rclone 1.75.1 ships in the image** and is what the wizard and the rclone services use. A remote you wrote into the rclone config yourself keeps working.
